name: first-campaign-regional
about: A carrier with no history: the pack holds the job and the benchmark only.

area.label: Fixture Yard, IL
area.reason: Fixture: drivers within a day's drive of the yard.

subject_matter.in_our_words: A small fleet where dispatch knows your name

history.text: Boostpoint 2026 benchmark, CDL drivers on Meta: an ad costing more than $42.00 per lead after 5 leads, or $85.00 spent with no lead, is where pausing is suggested.

output.audience: Class A drivers who meet the experience requirement and run flatbed, living in or near the Midwest lanes. Many are likely out for long stretches or in a large fleet with shared trucks. A plain pay per mile, weekly home time and an assigned truck would make them stop.

angles.idea: Lead with the pay per mile, stated plainly, over a loaded flatbed rolling on a Midwest highway.
angles.proof: The opening states its pay per mile, and the work is flatbed on Midwest lanes.
angles.why: Pay is the fact drivers compare most directly. Nothing has been measured for this carrier yet, so this is a starting test to judge against the benchmark cost per lead.

angles.idea: Lead with being home weekly, shown as a quiet home street at the end of a regional run.
angles.proof: The opening offers home weekly, and the job is regional on Midwest lanes.
angles.why: Home time is a main reason a driver looks at regional work, and the Midwest lanes make it believable. There are no earlier ads to compare, so this is untested.

angles.idea: Lead with the assigned truck: a parked flatbed rig that stays with its driver, in a small fleet where dispatch knows your name.
angles.proof: The job lists an assigned truck, flatbed work, and a small fleet where dispatch knows your name.
angles.why: An assigned truck and a small fleet are what set this job apart from a large carrier. There is no history yet, so it runs as a test beside the pay and home-time angles.

angles.idea: Say plainly who the job is for: Class A drivers with the stated experience who want flatbed work on Midwest lanes.
angles.proof: The opening is Class A regional, states its experience requirement, and is flatbed on Midwest lanes.
angles.why: Stating licence, experience, equipment and area up front should keep out drivers who cannot qualify or live elsewhere. With no lead outcomes yet, this is a precaution, not a proven result.

angles.idea: Set out the stated terms as a plain list: pay per mile, home weekly, the retirement plan and the assigned truck.
angles.proof: Each line is a fact of the opening: the pay per mile, home weekly, the retirement plan and the assigned truck.
angles.why: A plain list lets a driver check the whole offer at a glance, with no picture doing the selling. Nothing has been measured, so it is a test against the other angles.
